senses.gloss: To take complete control of someone's mind or behavior, as a spirit or a strange impulse is said to do.
senses.ru: овладевать (кем-л.), овладеть; вселяться (о духе); находить (что на тебя нашло)
examples: What *possessed* you to tell her that?
In the movie a demon *possesses* the youngest child.
He tore through the house like a man *possessed*.

senses.gloss: To send someone to a particular place to work or to stand guard.
senses.ru: назначать (на должность, в место службы), направлять; выставлять (охрану)
examples: The Army *posted* him to Germany for three years.
They *post* a guard at the gate every night.
She has been *posted* overseas twice since 2019.

senses.gloss: To officially announce a financial result such as a profit or a loss.
examples: The airline *posted* a record profit last quarter.
Analysts expect the company to *post* another loss.
The chain has *posted* three straight quarters of growth.

senses.gloss: To pay money to a court so that an accused person can stay out of jail until the trial.
examples: His brother *posted* bail the same night.
She could not afford to *post* a $10,000 bond.
Bail was *posted* by an anonymous donor.

senses.gloss: To beat hard and fast, said of your heart, or to throb with pain, said of your head.
senses.ru: колотиться, сильно биться (о сердце); раскалываться, ныть (о голове)
examples: My heart was *pounding* as I walked out on stage.
His head *pounded* all afternoon.
I could feel my pulse *pound* in my ears.

senses.gloss: To rain very hard.
senses.ru: лить как из ведра, хлестать (о дожде)
examples: It *poured* all weekend.
Don't go out right now — it's *pouring*.
If it *pours* again tonight, the game is off.

senses.gloss: To work in a profession such as law or medicine.
examples: She *practices* law in Chicago.
He *practiced* medicine in the same town for forty years.
You cannot *practice* here without a state license.

senses.gloss: To follow the customs and rules of a religion.
examples: Her family has *practiced* Buddhism for three generations.
Fewer young people *practice* the faith they were raised in.
He was brought up Catholic but stopped *practicing* in college.

senses.gloss: To get yourself or someone else ready for something that is going to happen.
examples: We spent all summer *preparing* for the move.
The school *prepared* the students for the state exam.
Nothing can *prepare* you for news like that.

senses.gloss: To state officially what must be done or how it must be done.
examples: The law *prescribes* a minimum sentence of five years.
The manual *prescribed* exactly how the tanks were to be cleaned.
Meetings must be held at the times *prescribed* in the bylaws.

senses.gloss: To cause a problem, a risk, or an opportunity to exist for someone.
senses.ru: представлять собой (проблему, опасность); создавать, создать (трудности, возможность)
examples: The delay *presents* a serious problem for the whole crew.
The storm *presented* rescue teams with a new set of dangers.
The scandal has *presented* her opponent with a rare opening.

senses.gloss: To keep urging someone strongly to do or say something.
examples: She *pressed* him to take the job.
Reporters kept *pressing* the governor about the missing files.
When *pressed*, he admitted he had never read the report.

senses.gloss: To dare to do something you have no right to do.
senses.ru: осмеливаться, осмелиться; позволять себе, брать на себя смелость
examples: I wouldn't *presume* to tell you how to run your own shop.
She *presumed* to speak for the whole department.
No one has ever *presumed* to question his figures.

senses.gloss: To write words using separate letters rather than joined cursive.
examples: Please *print* your name at the top of the form.
He *printed* the address in careful block capitals.
She was still *printing* every letter in second grade.

senses.gloss: To take the time to accept and come to terms with a difficult experience or feeling.
senses.ru: осмысливать, осмыслить; переваривать (пережитое), справляться с эмоциями
examples: I need a few days to *process* what happened.
She is still *processing* the news.
We never really *processed* the loss as a family.

senses.gloss: To push someone or something with your finger or with a pointed object.
examples: She *prodded* him in the ribs to wake him up.
The doctor kept *prodding* the sore spot to find the cause.
Don't *prod* the fish with a fork or the juice runs out.

senses.gloss: To bring something out and show it.
examples: He *produced* a driver's license from his back pocket.
You have to be able to *produce* proof of insurance.
Having *produced* no receipt, she was refused a refund.

senses.gloss: To be in charge of the money and the organization behind a film, a show, or a record.
examples: She *produces* a late-night talk show.
He *produced* three albums for the band.
The film was *produced* on a shoestring budget.

senses.gloss: To treat someone as a likely criminal because of their race or appearance rather than their behavior.
senses.ru: выделять по расовому признаку, применять расовое профилирование
examples: He says he was *profiled* because of the car he was driving.
The department denies that its officers *profile* drivers.
Critics accused the agency of *profiling* passengers by name and nationality.

senses.gloss: To estimate what a future figure or result will be.
examples: The city *projects* a shortfall of four million dollars next year.
Sales were *projected* to double, and they never did.
Forecasters are *projecting* a mild winter.

senses.gloss: To give other people a particular impression of yourself.
senses.ru: производить впечатление, создавать образ; излучать (уверенность, спокойствие)
examples: A good teacher *projects* calm even when things go wrong.
He *projected* a confidence he did not really feel.
She has always *projected* the image of someone in total control.

senses.gloss: To show signs that something is likely to happen.
examples: This *promises* to be the closest election in years.
The morning *promised* a hot day.
Dark clouds were building over the ridge, *promising* rain by noon.

senses.gloss: To cause someone to decide to do something.
senses.ru: побуждать, побудить; подталкивать (к действию); служить поводом
examples: The letter *prompted* him to call his sister after ten years.
One bad review can *prompt* a restaurant to change its whole menu.
The crash has *prompted* calls for tighter rules.

senses.gloss: To remind a performer or a speaker of words they have forgotten.
examples: Someone offstage *prompted* her when she froze.
The teacher had to *prompt* him twice during the recital.
He got through the whole speech without being *prompted* once.

senses.gloss: To declare something officially and formally.
examples: The doctor *pronounced* him dead at 3:40 a.m.
I now *pronounce* you husband and wife.
The building was *pronounced* unsafe and closed off.

senses.gloss: To let dough rise, or to get yeast working in warm liquid, before baking.
examples: *Proof* the yeast in warm water for about ten minutes.
I *proofed* the dough overnight in the refrigerator.
The rolls are still *proofing* on top of the stove.

senses.gloss: To travel outward through a space or a system, or to pass something on that way.
senses.ru: распространять(ся), распространить(ся); передавать(ся) (о волнах, сигнале, ошибке)
examples: Sound *propagates* faster in water than in air.
The error *propagated* through every report built on that file.
A crack can *propagate* through the metal for years before it fails.

senses.gloss: To force something open or loose with a tool or with your fingers.
examples: He *pried* the lid off with a screwdriver.
Firefighters had to *pry* the door open.
One board had been *pried* loose from the fence.

senses.gloss: To injure a muscle by stretching it too far.
examples: He *pulled* a hamstring in the first inning.
Bend your knees or you'll *pull* something.
She has *pulled* the same muscle twice this season.

senses.gloss: To carry out something sneaky, risky, or surprising.
examples: Don't ever *pull* a stunt like that again.
He *pulled* a prank on his roommate the first night.
The kids are always *pulling* something on the substitute teacher.

senses.gloss: To make a hole in paper, a card, or thin material with a tool.
examples: The conductor *punched* our tickets.
*Punch* three holes along the side of the box.
The card had been *punched* in the wrong place.

senses.gloss: To interrupt something again and again at intervals.
examples: Applause *punctuated* the speech every few minutes.
Long silences *punctuate* their phone calls.
The night was *punctuated* by the sound of sirens.

senses.gloss: To decide not to deal with something now and to leave it for later or for someone else.
senses.ru: откладывать (решение), отложить; пасовать, уходить от ответа
examples: Let's *punt* on that until we have real numbers.
The committee *punted*, sending the whole bill back to staff.
Congress has *punted* on the issue three years running.

senses.gloss: To work steadily at something you want to achieve over a long time.
examples: She left the firm to *pursue* a degree in nursing.
He *pursued* a career in music for a decade before giving it up.
The family is *pursuing* legal action against the hospital.

senses.gloss: To urge someone hard to do something, often harder than they want.
examples: My parents *pushed* me to apply to medical school.
A good coach knows how hard to *push* a player.
She felt *pushed* into a decision she wasn't ready to make.

senses.gloss: To sell illegal drugs.
examples: He was arrested for *pushing* heroin.
They *pushed* pills out of a rented garage for two years.
Nobody would dare *push* drugs that close to a school.

senses.gloss: To add something to a statement so that it is less strong or less general.
examples: I'd *qualify* that a little: it works, but only on new machines.
He *qualified* his praise with a warning about the cost.
Every promise in the letter is *qualified* by a footnote.

senses.gloss: To ask a question about something because you think it may be wrong.
senses.ru: спрашивать, ставить под сомнение; оспаривать (счёт, цифры)
examples: She *queried* the extra charge on her bill.
If a number looks off, *query* it before you sign anything.
Two of the figures have been *queried* by the auditor.

senses.gloss: To beat very fast, said of your heart, or to run wildly, said of your thoughts.
senses.ru: колотиться, бешено биться (о сердце); лихорадочно работать (о мыслях)
examples: My heart was *racing* by the time I reached the door.
His mind *raced* through everything that could go wrong.
Coffee that late makes my pulse *race*.

senses.gloss: To go into a place and help yourself to what is in it, especially food or money.
senses.ru: опустошать, опустошить (холодильник); залезать, залезть (в сбережения, фонд)
examples: The kids *raided* the fridge the minute they got home.
He had to *raid* his savings to pay for the repair.
The pension fund had been *raided* years before anyone noticed.

senses.gloss: To bring up a subject, a question, or an objection so that people will deal with it.
examples: She *raised* the issue at the last meeting.
Nobody wanted to *raise* the question of money.
Several parents have *raised* concerns about the new schedule.
